claims.statement: All curated tool modules live flat under agent/tools/ and are re-exported through agent/tools/__init__.py, which lazily imports and caches each export from _TOOL_MODULES; its custom _LazyToolsModule prevents same-named imported submodules from shadowing public tool exports.

For an executable thread, agent/server.py:get_agent assembles the main coding agent's static tools for web access, plan lifecycle, background execution, user configuration, Linear, threads, baby-sit, notifications, PR creation/review, recovery, scheduling, reporting, and Slack.

The main agent's static tool list is context-sensitive: admin threads add ADMIN_TOOLS, sandbox download tools are conditional, local_run collapses to http_request/fetch_url/web_search, stop_summary collapses to Slack read/reply, and Slack tools are removed when Slack is unavailable.

The main agent exposes Observability, Currents, Notion, available Browser tools, and optionally Corridor as DynamicToolMiddleware integration groups; integration schemas are loaded by load_integration_tools for a later model turn, and unavailable loads return tool errors rather than failing the run.

agent/reviewer.py:get_reviewer_agent wires curated review tools fetch_review_diff, add_finding, update_finding, list_findings, publish_review, resolve_finding_thread, reply_to_finding_thread, plus web_search, fetch_url, and http_request; it does not wire open_pull_request as a curated reviewer tool.
agent/analyzer.py:get_analyzer runs a minimal graph exposing only save_review_style_prompt and read_finding_outcomes.

agent/chat.py defines a separate read-only PR chat agent that uses GitHub-API-backed read tools (read_repo_file and search_repo_code), list_review_findings, and web tools, while excluding mutating sandbox built-ins and giving its subagent a read-only filesystem allowlist.

Plan mode is enforced by PlanModeMiddleware using PLAN_MODE_EXCLUDED_TOOLS; it is installed unconditionally and is state-aware, so it restricts tools after a mid-run enter_plan_mode call as well as when a run starts in plan mode.

PLAN_MODE_EXCLUDED_TOOLS removes side-effecting tools during planning, including task, background work, browser actions, HTTP requests, PR/thread/sandbox/skill/Slack/Linear/environment mutations, and automation mutations, while list_threads, get_thread, and built-in file and shell tools remain available.

The lazy tool catalog exports five automation operations from .automations and read_user_settings, but automation management is attached only through ADMIN_TOOLS while read_user_settings is a normal main-agent static tool.

Automation tools enforce admin authorization and wrap the dashboard schedule service: creation uses the verified admin identity, updates reject contradictory clear/set arguments, triggers can run paused automations, and operations return structured errors rather than propagating service exceptions.

read_user_settings derives all identities from verified thread participants and returns safe profile settings, instructions, and redacted integration connection statuses without tokens or credentials.
PlanModeMiddleware resets the plan_mode state at each run to its configured initial value, avoiding stale persisted state while still responding to a mid-run Command before the next model call.

DynamicToolMiddleware rejects integration-name collisions with the loader, static reserved names, and other integrations; it builds each group once under a per-group lock, caches resolution, and resets loaded tool names before each agent run.

SanitizeToolInputsMiddleware repairs only malformed read_file offset and limit arguments by extracting a leading integer before validation, and is installed on the main, reviewer, analyzer, and chat graphs.

http_request and fetch_url use safe redirect handling; http_request offloads serialized responses larger than 100,000 characters to sandbox JSONL, while focused tests cover blocking private and metadata addresses and redirects before a request is issued.

Corridor's deferred MCP loader requires a token and a fixed HTTPS Corridor endpoint, sends its bearer token from the LangGraph server process rather than the sandbox, allowlists analyzePlan, and degrades connection errors to no tools.
ExcludeToolsMiddleware filters named tools on every model request and is designed to run after tool-injecting middleware so it can remove built-in or subagent-injected tools.
